q: DELAY : EXPEDITE –
e: To delay is to slow something down, and to expedite is to speed it up, so the words are opposites. In the same way, to detain is to hold someone back, and to dispatch is to send someone off quickly.

q: ANARCHY : GOVERNMENT –
e: Anarchy is the absence of government. In the same way, penury (extreme poverty) is the absence of wealth.

q: VACCINE : PREVENT –
e: A vaccine is used to prevent a disease. In the same way, an antidote is used to counteract a poison. Both pairs show an object and its purpose.

q: ____ glass is, for all practical, a solid, its molecular structure is that of a liquid.
e: The sentence shows a contrast: glass behaves like a solid, yet its structure is that of a liquid. "Although" introduces such a contrast.

q: An intensive search was conducted by the detective to locate those criminals, who ______.
e: The criminals escaped before the search was conducted. An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect tense, so "had escaped" is correct.

q: The intellectual can no longer be said to live ____ the margins of society.
e: "Beyond the margins of society" means outside or apart from mainstream society. The sentence says intellectuals can no longer be seen as living outside society.

q: According to the conditions of my scholarship, after finishing my degree ____.
o: my education will be employed by the University.
employment will be given to me by the University.
I will be employed of the University.
e: "The University will employ me" is a clear active sentence with correct grammar. Options ক and খ are awkward passive forms, and ঘ uses the wrong preposition "of" instead of "by".

q: If a substance is cohesive, it tends to ____.
e: "Cohesive" means having the quality of sticking together. So a cohesive substance tends to stick together.

q: He stopped his car ____ when the light turned red.
e: "Abruptly" means suddenly and without warning. A driver stops suddenly when the light turns red, so "abruptly" fits.

q: The influence of the technological revolution in ____ and ____ the concentration of wealth and power in the hands of the few should worry us all.
e: The sentence says the influence should worry us all, so the technological revolution must be increasing the concentration of wealth. "Accelerating" and "intensifying" both mean increasing, which fits.

q: Few people would care to take the negative side of the proposition that the women of the world are ____ and ____.
e: Few people would argue against a proposition only if it is widely accepted as true. The common view is that women of the world have been oppressed and scorned, so this pair fits.

q: Anger, even when it is - has one virtue, it overcomes ____.
e: The sentence admits that anger is bad but says it has one virtue. "Sinful" fits the first blank, and anger overcomes "sloth" (laziness), which is a real virtue of anger.

q: The word ‘dilly dally’ means –
e: "Dilly-dally" means to waste time through delay or indecision.

q: The word ‘Euphemism’ means –
o: description of a disagreeable thing by an agreeable name
contrast of words is made in the same sentence
a statement is made emphatic by overstatement
e: A euphemism is a mild or pleasant word used in place of a harsh or unpleasant one. For example, "passed away" is a euphemism for "died".

q: The passive form of the sentence ‘some children were helping the wounded man’-
o: The wounded man was helped by some children
The wounded man was helping some children
The wounded man was being helped by some children
The wounded man was to be helped by some children
e: The active sentence is in the past continuous tense. Its passive form uses "was/were being + past participle", so "The wounded man was being helped by some children" is correct.

q: ‘Rumor is the most primitive way of spreading stories-by passing them on from mouth to mouth. But civilized countries in normal times have better Sources of news than rumor. They have radio, television, and newspapers. In times of stress and confusion, however, rumor emerges and becomes rife. At such times different kinds of news are in competition: the press, television, and radio versus the grape vine. Especially do rumors spread when war requires censorship on many important matters. The customary news Sources no longer give out enough information. Since the people cannot learn through legitimate channels all that they are anxious to learn, they pick up ‘news’ whenever they can and when this happens, rumor thrives. Rumors are often repeated even by those who do not believe the tales. There is a fascination about them. The reason is that the cleverly designed rumor gives expression to something deep in the hearts of the victims-the fears, suspicions, forbidden hopes, or daydreams which they hesitate to voice directly. Pessimistic rumors about defeat and disasters show that the people who repeat them are worried and anxious. Optimistic rumors about record production or peace soon coming paint to complacency or confidence-and often to overconfidence.’
e: The passage explains why rumor arises, when it spreads and what it reveals about people's fears and hopes. So the passage deals with the nature of rumor as a whole. The question stem seems to be missing from this item.

q: The author suggests that rumors usually-
e: The author says that in times of stress rumor "emerges and becomes rife" and "thrives". This shows that rumors grow strongly and are hard to stop, so they are hardy in their growth.

q: The author states that during wartime the regular sources of news present only –
e: The passage says that during war "the customary news sources no longer give out enough information" because of censorship. So they present only limited information.

q: Which of the following best describes the author’s personal attitude toward rumor?
e: The author calmly analyses why rumors spread and what they reveal about human feelings, without anger or excitement. This is a philosophical interest in the subject.

q: Many companies now have employee assistance programs that enable employees, free of charge, to improve their physical fitness, reduce stress, and learn ways to stop smoking. These programs increase worker productivity, reduce absenteeism and lessen insurance costs for employee health care. Therefore, these programs benefit the company as well as the employee. ____ Which of the following, if true, most significantly strengthens the conclusion above?
o: Physical fitness programs are often the most popular services offered to employees.
Studies have shown that training in stress management is not effective for many people.
Regular exercise reduces people’s risk of heart disease and provides them with increased energy
Employee assistance programs require companies to hire people to supervise the various programs offered.
e: The conclusion says the programs benefit the company as well as the employee. If regular exercise lowers the risk of heart disease and gives more energy, workers become healthier and more productive, which directly supports that claim. Option ক only shows popularity, while খ and ঘ weaken the argument.

q: Choose the answer that is closest in meaning to the following sentence: ”Despite the great difference in size, shape and function, all human cells have the same 46 chromosomes.”
o: All human cells are the same because the 46 chromosomes govern size, shape and function.
Difference in size, shape and function are not very great because all human cells have the same 46 chromosomes.
The size, shape and function of human cells are the same, but the 46 chromosomes are different.
Although the 46 chromosomes are the same in all human cells, there are difference in the size, shape and function.
e: The original sentence says that cells differ in size, shape and function, yet all have the same 46 chromosomes. Option ঘ keeps both facts and the contrast between them. The other options either deny the differences or wrongly say the chromosomes differ.

q: In the following four questions, choose the word or phrase that is most nearly similar or opposite in meaning to the word given in the question:- INFRINGE
e: "Infringe" means to break a rule or law, or to go beyond a limit. "Transgress" has the same meaning, so it is the closest word.

q: BROCHURE
e: A "brochure" is a small booklet that gives information or advertises something. "Pamphlet" means the same thing.

q: EQUIVOCAL
e: "Equivocal" means unclear or open to more than one interpretation. Its opposite is "clear".

q: ILLUSIVE
e: "Illusive" means deceptive, based on illusion. So its opposite meaning is "not deceptive".

q: In the following three questions, a related pair of words is followed by four pairs of word. Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to the expressed in the original pair: CARPENTER : SAW
e: A carpenter uses a saw as a cutting tool in his work. In the same way a seamstress uses scissors to cut cloth. A brush is a tool too, but it is not for cutting, so the seamstress pair matches best.

q: FIRE : ASHES
e: Ashes are what remain after a fire is over. In the same way, memories are what remain after an event has passed.

q: STARE : GLANCE
e: To stare is to look long, and to glance is to look briefly. In the same way, to gulp is to drink in a large amount, and to sip is to drink a small amount. Both pairs show a big and a small form of the same action.

q: Each sentence below has two blanks. Choose the set of words for each blank that best fits the meaning of the sentence as a whole: Although a few years ago the fundamental fact about the milky way seemed fairly well _____ now even its mass and radius have come into ______.
e: "Although" sets up a contrast: facts that once seemed well established are now uncertain. "Established" fits the first blank, and "come into question" means become doubtful, which fits the second.

q: Because she had reputation for ___ we were surprised and pleased when she greeted us so____.
e: The speakers were surprised, so her reputation must be the opposite of how she greeted them. "Querulousness" means a habit of complaining, and "affably" means in a friendly way, so this pair creates the needed contrast.

q: A ____ statement is an ____ comparison; it does not compare. Things explicitly but suggest a likeness between them.
e: A metaphor compares two things without using "like" or "as". So a metaphorical statement is an implied comparison, not an explicit one.

q: Choose the word or phrase that best fill the blank space to complete the sentences: If a ruby is heated it ___ temporarily lose its color.
e: This sentence states a general scientific fact, so the first conditional with "will" in the main clause fits: "If a ruby is heated, it will temporarily lose its colour."

q: All of the people at the AAME conference are -
e: The subject is "Mathematics", which is a singular noun ending in "s". When it modifies another noun it keeps its form, and "all of the people" needs a plural noun. So "Mathematics teachers" is correct.

q: Prices for bicycles can run ____ TK. 2,000.00.
e: The expression "as high as" is used to show an upper limit of an amount. So prices can run as high as Tk. 2,000.

q: Travellers ____ their reservations well in advance if they want to fly during the Eid holidays.
e: "Had better" is followed by the base form of the verb without "to". So "had better get" is correct.

q: A seventeen year old is not - to vote in an election.
e: "Enough" comes after an adjective. So the correct order is "old enough", not "enough old".

q: Almost everyone fails - on the first try.
o: to have passed his driver’s test
e: The verb "fail" is followed by a to-infinitive: someone fails to do something. So the correct phrase is "fails to pass his driver's test"; option খ seems to have lost the word "pass". "Fails in passing" is not standard usage.

q: Throughout history, the search for salt has played an important role in society. Where it was scarce, salt was traded ounce for ounce with gold. Rome’s major highway was called the via salaria, that is the Salt Road. Along the road, Roman soldiers transported salt crystals from the salt flats at Ostia up the Tiber River. In return, they received a salarium or salary literally money paid to soldiers to buy salt. The old saying ”worth their salt” which to be valuable derives from the custom of payment during the Empire. What does the passage mainly discuss?
e: Every sentence of the passage talks about salt: its value, the Salt Road, salary and the saying "worth their salt". So the main topic is salt.

q: According to the passage salt flats were located in-
e: The passage says Roman soldiers carried salt crystals "from the salt flats at Ostia". So the salt flats were at Ostia.

q: Salarium is a Latin word that means –
e: According to the passage, soldiers received a "salarium" or salary, which was money paid to buy salt. So "salarium" means salary.

q: If a man is,’worth his salt.’ he is-
e: The passage explains that "worth their salt" means to be valuable. So a man who is worth his salt is a valuable employee who deserves his pay.

q: ‘সততা সর্বোৎকৃষ্ট পন্থা’ – কোনটির অনুবাদ?
e: "সততা সর্বোৎকৃষ্ট পন্থা" একটি প্রবাদ, এর প্রচলিত ইংরেজি রূপ "Honesty is the best policy"। এখানে "পন্থা" মানে নীতি বা কৌশল, তাই policy শব্দটি বসে।

q: The sentence with correct punctuations-
o: Maria, my student, is on leave to-day.
Maria my student, is on leave to-day.
Maria my student is on leave to-day.
Maria my student is, on leave to-day.
e: "my student" is an appositive that explains who Maria is, so it must be set off by commas on both sides. Only option ক places a comma before and after the appositive.

q: The antonym for ‘Inimical’-
e: "Inimical" means hostile or harmful. Its opposite is "friendly". "Hostile" is a synonym, not an antonym.

q: The synonym for ‘efface’-
e: "Efface" means to erase or rub something out so that it disappears. So "rub out" is the closest meaning.

q: The best passive form of the sentence: ‘We don’t like idle people’-
o: We are not liked by idle people.
Idle people are not like us.
Idle people are not liked by us.
Idle people are not of our liking.
e: In the active sentence "we" is the subject and "idle people" is the object. In passive voice the object becomes the subject and the verb takes "be + past participle": "Idle people are not liked by us."

q: The correct sentence of the followings-
o: The Nile is longest river in Africa.
The Nile is Longest river in the Africa.
Nile is longest river in Africa.
The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
e: The names of rivers take the definite article "the", and a superlative adjective like "longest" also needs "the". Names of continents such as Africa take no article. So "The Nile is the longest river in Africa" is correct.

q: Browning was the composer of any of the following poems-
e: "Andrea del Sarto" is a famous dramatic monologue by Robert Browning. "The Scholar Gipsy" is by Matthew Arnold, and "The Two Voices" is by Tennyson.

q: The right word to fill in the gap of the following sentence- ‘Give her a telephone number to ring ____ she gets lost’-
e: "In case" is used to talk about a precaution taken against a possible future event. The number is given beforehand as a safeguard for the possibility that she gets lost, so "in case" fits.

q: The synonym of ‘Franchise’ –
e: "Franchise" means a special right or privilege, such as the right to vote or a licence to sell a company's goods. So "privilege" is the closest meaning.

q: The opposite word of ‘sluggish’-
e: "Sluggish" means slow and lacking energy. Its opposite is "animated", which means lively and full of energy. "Dull", "heavy" and "slow" are close in meaning to sluggish.

q: The correct spelling is-
e: The correct spelling is "humorous". When the suffix "-ous" is added to "humour", the "u" before "r" is dropped.

q: ‘Equivocation’ means-
o: Equal opportunity to get a job
Two contrary things in the same statement
e: "Equivocation" means using unclear or double-meaning language to avoid committing oneself to the truth. Such a statement can be read in two contrary ways, so option ঘ fits best.

q: When a person says he’s all in’, it means-
e: The informal phrase "all in" means completely exhausted. So when a person says "he's all in", it means he is very tired.

q: ‘Bill of fare’ is-
o: A list of dishes at a restaurant
e: "Bill of fare" is an old term for a menu. It is the list of dishes served at a restaurant.

q: A ‘bull market’ means that share prices are-
e: A "bull market" is a period when share prices keep rising and investors are optimistic. The opposite is a "bear market", when prices fall.

q: ‘Blue chips’ are-
o: Industrial shares considered to be a safe investment
Industrial shares considered to be a risky investment
A list of dishes at a restaurant
e: "Blue chips" are shares of large, well-established and financially sound companies. They are considered a safe investment.

q: ‘Razzmatazz’ means-
e: "Razzmatazz" means noisy, showy and exciting activity meant to attract attention. So "a noisy activity" is the best meaning.

q: ‘Blockbuster’ means-
o: A large solid piece of store
A device to cut off a person’s head as a punishment
A powerful explosive to demolish buildings
e: The word "blockbuster" originally meant a very powerful bomb that could destroy a whole city block. Today it also means a hugely successful film or book.

q: Any one of the following pairs are literary collaborators-
e: T. S. Eliot and Ezra Pound worked closely together. Pound edited Eliot's manuscript of "The Waste Land" heavily, and Eliot dedicated the poem to him as "il miglior fabbro".

q: The correct sentence of the followings-
o: A new cabinet has been sworn in in Dhaka.
A new cabinet has been sworn in Dhaka.
A new cabinet has been sworn by in Dhaka.
A new cabinet has sworn in Dhaka.
e: "Sworn in" is a phrasal verb meaning formally installed in office by taking an oath. Then "in Dhaka" names the place, so the two "in"s sit side by side: "has been sworn in in Dhaka".

q: ‘To read between the lines’ means-
o: To read quickly to save time
To read carefully to find out any hidden meaning
e: "To read between the lines" means to look for a hidden meaning that is not stated directly. So option ঘ is correct.

q: The last word of the proverb, ‘Handsome is that handsome__.’
e: The full proverb is "Handsome is that handsome does". It means a person is judged by good deeds, not by good looks.

q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: I forbade him not to go
e: The verb "forbid" takes an object followed by a to-infinitive: "forbid someone to do something". "Forbade" already carries a negative sense, so adding "not" is wrong.

q: Which of the following is a correct proverb?
o: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.
Fools rush in where an angel fears to tread.
A fool rushes in where an angle fears to tread.
Fools rush in where the angels fear to tread.
e: The fixed form of the proverb is "Fools rush in where angels fear to tread." It means foolish people act hastily in situations that wise people avoid.

q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: Why did you have done this?
e: A wh-question needs the auxiliary before the subject. "Why have you done this?" follows this order and uses the present perfect correctly. Options ক and ঘ keep statement word order, and "did you have done" mixes two tenses.

q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: That shirt which he bought is blue in colour.
The shirt that which he bought is blue in colour.
Which shirt he bought is blue in colour.
The shirt which he bought is blue in colour.
e: "The shirt which he bought" correctly uses the definite article with a relative clause. Option খ repeats "that which", and option ক uses "that" where "the" is needed.

q: The correct passive of ‘Sheila was writing a letter’ is –
o: A letter was writing by sheila.
A letter was being writing by sheila
A letter was being written by sheila
A letter was been written by sheila
e: The active verb "was writing" is past continuous. Its passive form is "was being + past participle", so the correct passive is "A letter was being written by Sheila."

q: Which of the following sentences is correct?
o: One of my friends are a lawyer
One of my friends is a lawyer
One of my friend is a lawyer
One of my friends are lawyers
e: In "one of + plural noun", the real subject is "one", which is singular. So the verb must be singular: "One of my friends is a lawyer."

q: The word ‘ecological’ is related to –
e: Ecological relates to ecology, the study of how living things interact with each other and their environment. So it is related to the environment.

q: The synonym of ‘genesis’ is –
e: Genesis means the origin or beginning of something. Preface, foreword and introduction refer to the opening part of a book, not to origin.

q: The word ‘homogeneous’ means –
e: Homogeneous means made up of parts that are all of the same kind. Its opposite is heterogeneous, meaning of different kinds.

q: The word ‘imbibe’ means—
e: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol. In a figurative sense it also means to absorb ideas, but the basic meaning is "to drink".

q: Something which is obnoxious means that it is –
e: Obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or offensive. So "very unpleasant" is correct.

q: A pilgrim is a person who undertakes a journey to a –
e: A pilgrim is a person who travels to a holy place for religious reasons. A mosque can be one such place, but "holy place" covers the full meaning.

q: Shakespeare is known mostly for his –
e: William Shakespeare is known mainly for his plays, such as "Hamlet", "Macbeth" and "Romeo and Juliet". He also wrote 154 sonnets, but his fame rests on drama.

q: A person who writes about his own life writes –
e: An autobiography is the story of a person's life written by that person. A biography is written by someone else.

q: In Which century was the Victorian period ?
e: The Victorian period covers the reign of Queen Victoria, from 1837 to 1901. So it falls in the 19th century.

q: The antonym of ‘indifference’ is –
e: Indifference means a lack of interest or feeling. Ardour means strong enthusiasm or passion, so it is the clearest opposite.

q: Three score is –
e: A score means twenty. So three score means three times twenty, that is sixty.

q: An Ordinance is –
e: An ordinance is an official order or law made by a government authority. In Bangladesh, the President can issue an ordinance when Parliament is not in session.

q: A fantasy is—
e: A fantasy is an imaginary story or idea that is far from reality. So "an imaginary story" is correct.

q: Something that is ‘fresh’ is something –
e: Fresh means new, not stale, and in good condition, such as fresh fruit. Among the options, "in fairly good condition" comes closest.

q: The speaker failed to make the audience ______ to him patiently. – Which of the following is the correct verb form in the blank above
e: After the causative verb "make" in the active voice, we use the bare infinitive without "to". So "make the audience listen" is correct.

q: Which of the following ages in literary history is the latest?
e: The Restoration Age began in 1660, the Augustan Age covers the early 18th century, and the Victorian Age runs from 1837 to 1901. The Georgian Age (in poetry, around 1910-1936) comes after these, so it is the latest.

q: The first English dictionary was compiled by-
e: Samuel Johnson's "A Dictionary of the English Language" (1755) is regarded as the first major and complete English dictionary. That is why he is named as the compiler of the first English dictionary.

q: My uncle has three sons, ____ work in the same office. Which of the following is the best form of pronoun in the above sentence?
e: The sentence joins two clauses with a comma, so it needs a relative pronoun, not a personal pronoun. "All of whom" refers back to "three sons" and joins the clauses correctly.

q: People always remember patriots. Which of the following is the best passive form of the above sentence?
o: The patriots will always be remembered by people
The patriots are always being remembered
People are always remembered by The patriots
e: In the passive voice, the object "patriots" becomes the subject and the verb becomes "are remembered". The agent "by people" is general, so it can be dropped: "The patriots are always remembered."

q: What is the meaning of the word ‘intrepid’?
e: Intrepid means fearless and brave, especially in facing danger. Belligerent means eager to fight, which is different.

q: What is the meaning of the expression ‘bottom line’?
o: The last line of a book
e: "Bottom line" means the most important or essential point of a matter. It originally referred to the final line of a financial statement showing profit or loss.

q: The word ‘plurality’ means-
o: The holding of more than one office at a time
e: One meaning of plurality is the holding of two or more offices or positions at the same time. It also means a large number or the state of being plural.

q: ‘Pediatric’ relates to the treatment of –
e: Pediatric relates to the medical care of children. A pediatrician is a doctor for children, while geriatrics deals with old people.

q: ‘Boot leg’ means to-
e: To bootleg means to make, carry or sell goods, especially alcohol, illegally. So it is closest to "smuggle".

q: Are you doing anything special ____ the weekend? -fill in the gap with appropriate preposition.
e: In British English, "at the weekend" is the standard phrase, while American English uses "on the weekend". The expected answer here follows British usage.

q: Which of the following is a correct sentence?
o: He was too clever not to miss the point
He was to clever to miss the point
He was too clever to miss the point
He was too clever to grasp the point
e: "Too ... to" carries a negative meaning. "He was too clever to miss the point" means he was so clever that he could not miss the point. Option ক adds an extra "not", and option খ misspells "too".

q: The ‘Poet Laureate’ is-
o: the best poet of the country
a winner of the Noble Prize in poetry
e: The Poet Laureate is a poet officially appointed by the British monarch, originally to write poems for court and national occasions. So the term means the court poet of England.

q: Which of the following school of literary writings is connected with a medical theory?
e: The Comedy of Humours, made popular by Ben Jonson, is based on the old medical theory of four bodily fluids or "humours". An excess of one humour was thought to shape a person's character.

q: Who of the following was both a poet and painter?
e: William Blake was both a poet and a painter. He illustrated his own poems, such as "Songs of Innocence and of Experience", with engravings.

q: What is the synonym of ‘incredible’?
e: Incredible means impossible or hard to believe. So its synonym is "unbelievable".
